messages.subject: mediation model in lavaan
parts:
I am a newbie in lavaan and I am clueless of what I did is correct. I would appreciate any comment from people who are more knowledgeable. I am trying to replicate in R using lavaan a model I previously tested in AMOS (see attached AMOS path model). I am not sure though if my syntax in the model specification is correct. I would like to know why lavaan automatically correlates the residuals of my outcome variables? Also, how can I test for indirect effects. I want to be able to produce 90% bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals for the indirect effects. Thanks very much. Any comment would be greatly appreciated.

My model specification syntax
> ####variables
> #Anxiety = MEAN_GAD
> #Satisfaction with Life = MEAN_SLS
> #Self-Concept Clarity = MEAN_SCC
> #Commitment = MEAN_COM
> #Exploration = MEAN_EXP
> #Reconsideration of Commitment = MEAN_REC
> #Maternal Trust = MEAN_M_Tru
> #Maternal Communication = MEAN_M_Com
> #Paternal Trust = MEAN_P_Tru
> #Paternal Communication = MEAN_P_Com
> 
> PATH.model <-
+   '
+     #outcome variables
+     MEAN_GAD ~ MEAN_F_Com + MEAN_EXP + MEAN_REC
+     MEAN_SLS ~ MEAN_M_Tru + MEAN_M_Com + MEAN_F_Tru + MEAN_F_Com + MEAN_COM
+     MEAN_SCC ~ MEAN_M_Com + MEAN_EXP + MEAN_REC
+ 
+     #mediator variables
+     MEAN_COM ~ MEAN_M_Tru + MEAN_F_Tru
+     MEAN_EXP ~ MEAN_F_Tru
+     MEAN_REC ~ MEAN_M_Tru + MEAN_F_Tru + MEAN_F_Com
+ 
+     #correlated predictors
+     MEAN_M_Tru ~~ MEAN_M_Com
+     MEAN_M_Tru ~~ MEAN_F_Tru
+     MEAN_M_Tru ~~ MEAN_F_Com
+ 
+     MEAN_M_Com ~~ MEAN_F_Tru
+     MEAN_M_Com ~~ MEAN_F_Com
+ 
+     MEAN_F_Tru ~~ MEAN_F_Com
+ 
+     MEAN_COM ~~ MEAN_EXP
+     
+   '
> fitPATH <- sem(PATH.model, data = dataframe)

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: mediation model in lavaan
parts: > *What does this error message mean? Should I be concerned about this?*

> Warning message:
> In vnames(FLAT, "ov.x", warn = TRUE) :
> lavaan WARNING: model syntax contains variance/covariance/intercept
> formulas
> involving (an) exogenous variable(s): [MEAN_F_Com MEAN_M_Tru
> MEAN_M_Com MEAN_F_Tru];
> Please use fixed.x=FALSE or leave them alone

By default, lavaan treats exogenous variables as fixed. This means that
you do not need to specify their covariances. So, you can omit this part
of the model syntax:

# correlated predictors
MEAN_M_Tru ~~ MEAN_M_Com
MEAN_M_Tru ~~ MEAN_F_Tru
MEAN_M_Tru ~~ MEAN_F_Com

MEAN_M_Com ~~ MEAN_F_Tru
MEAN_M_Com ~~ MEAN_F_Com

MEAN_F_Tru ~~ MEAN_F_Com

MEAN_COM ~~ MEAN_EXP

But this will not affect the results.

> *Why does lavaan automatically correlate the residuals of my outcome
> variables?*

Because we believe it is a sensible thing to do. Of course, if you do
not like lavaan's defaults, you should use the lavaan() function instead.

To learn how to test for indirect effects, please read section 7.4 of
the lavaan paper (see lavaan.org website for the link), and see the
examples here:

http://www.da.ugent.be/cvs/pages/en/Presentations/Presentation%20Yves%20Rosseel.pdf

Yves.
